PREMIUM
WOOD VARNISH - CLEAR GLOSS
Clear Varnish

Superior scratch-resistant clear gloss

Quick-drying multipurpose clear varnish for interior woodwork. Blend of modified polyurethane alkyd resin and hardening agent that preserves the natural beauty of timber.

KEY FEATURES
Superior scratch resistant
Maximum durability
Fast dry time
High spreading capacity
Retains natural beauty of timber
TECHNICAL DATA
COVERAGE	12–15 m² per litre (on smooth, non-porous surfaces)
TOUCH DRY	3–4 hours
RECOAT	12–16 hours
FINISH	Clear gloss
THINNING	Cloud White Spirit
APPLICATION	Brush (working well into grain)
WHERE TO USE IT
Doors, trim, furniture and joinery
Counters and timber pelmets
Skirting boards and wall partitions
Interior woodwork requiring a clear protective finish
SUITABLE SURFACES
Interior woodwork · New timber · Previously varnished wood (properly prepared)
HOW TO APPLY
1
Prepare the surface

Ensure wood is clean, dust-free and defective or poorly adhering material removed. Rub down with abrasive paper and dust off.

2
Prime or undercoat

Apply a minimum of 3 coats Cloud Multipurpose Clear Varnish. On new bare timber, the first coat should be thinned to ease brushing consistency using Cloud White Spirit.

3
Apply the finish

By brush, working well into the surface to get good penetration and adhesion on wood. Not recommended for floors. Finish high gloss — the latter is not recommended for use on floors.

Previously painted: For previously varnished woodwork — unsound timber: remove all old and damaged varnish down to bare surface.  ·  Clean-up: Clean all equipment with Cloud White Spirit immediately after use.

HOW TO READ IT
Reading the chart

Every shade carries a code, and the code is the thing to quote at the counter. Names are easy to mishear, and more than one family has a shade people will call “the dusty rose”.

THE CODE

CP·RD010 breaks into three parts. CP is Cloud Paints. RD is the family — Reds & Crimsons. 010 is the position within that family.

Positions run 010 to 320 in steps of ten, palest to deepest. So CP·RD010 is the lightest red on the card and CP·RD320 the darkest, with thirty-two steps between. The same holds in all 17 families, which is why two shades the same distance down two different pages sit at about the same depth.

GETTING IT MIXED

Any shade here can be tinted onto our emulsions and enamels at the Industrial Area counter. Bring the code, the finish you want and the tin size. Tinted shades may carry a surcharge depending on the colourant.

Ready-mixed whites and standard colours are on the shelf and need no tinting — those are in the price list.

THE SAME LADDER IN EVERY FAMILY

Each strip is one family, all thirty-two steps in order. Position in the code is position on the strip, so CP·GN160 and CP·BL160 sit at the same depth as each other.

Colour changes with the light it is under and with the sheen it is mixed into: the same code reads deeper in matt than in silk, and a north-facing room will cool it. Look at a shade on the wall it is destined for, at the hour you will most often see it.

FINISHES & TEXTURES
Finish and texture

A colour is only half the decision. The same shade in matt and in high-gloss will not look like the same colour, and it will not wear the same way either.

Sheen levels

Sheen is how much light the dry film throws back. Low sheen hides an uneven wall; high sheen takes scrubbing.

FINISH	SHEEN	WHERE IT BELONGS
Matte	0–5% sheen	Ceilings, low-traffic walls, bedrooms. Hides surface flaws; softest look.
Eggshell	10–15%	Ceilings, low-traffic walls, bedrooms. Hides surface flaws; softest look.
Satin	25–35%	Living rooms, hallways, kids' rooms. Gentle glow, wipeable, everyday durable.
Silk	35–45%	Living rooms, hallways, kids' rooms. Gentle glow, wipeable, everyday durable.
Semi-Gloss	50–70%	Kitchens, bathrooms, doors, trim. Moisture-resistant and easy to scrub.
High-Gloss	85%+	Furniture, feature doors, metal. Hard, mirror-like, maximum protection.
Textured finishes

Applied by hand with a trowel, roller or sponge, so no two walls come out quite alike. Quoted separately from the tinted ranges.

TEXTURE	EFFECT
Suede	Feature walls - soft tactile matte finish.
Limewash	Old-world mottled plaster effect, breathable.
Sandstone	Fine grain natural stone look.
Concrete	Industrial polished raw-concrete read.
Metallic	Brushed metal shimmer accent.
Roller Stipple	Textured roller pattern, classic finish.

Sheen comes from the product, not from the tint. Silk Vinyl gives a silk finish, Vinyl Matt and SuperMatt a matt one, and Super Gloss or Gloss Enamel the high-sheen end. HOW TO READ IT
Reading the chart

Every shade carries a code, and the code is the thing to quote at the counter. Names are easy to mishear, and more than one family has a shade people will call “the dusty rose”.

THE CODE

CP·RD010 breaks into three parts. CP is Cloud Paints. RD is the family — Reds & Crimsons. 010 is the position within that family.

Positions run 010 to 320 in steps of ten, palest to deepest. So CP·RD010 is the lightest red on the card and CP·RD320 the darkest, with thirty-two steps between. The same holds in all 17 families, which is why two shades the same distance down two different pages sit at about the same depth.

GETTING IT MIXED

Any shade here can be tinted onto our emulsions and enamels at the Industrial Area counter. Bring the code, the finish you want and the tin size. Tinted shades may carry a surcharge depending on the colourant.

Ready-mixed whites and standard colours are on the shelf and need no tinting — those are in the price list.

FINISHES & TEXTURES
Finish and texture

A colour is only half the decision. The same shade in matt and in high-gloss will not look like the same colour, and it will not wear the same way either.

Sheen levels

Sheen is how much light the dry film throws back. Low sheen hides an uneven wall; high sheen takes scrubbing.

FINISH	SHEEN	WHERE IT BELONGS
Matte	0–5% sheen	Ceilings, low-traffic walls, bedrooms. Hides surface flaws; softest look.

1
Prepare the surface

Concrete must be fully cured (minimum 28 days). Remove all dust, laitance, oil and grease. Acid-etch or mechanically abrade smooth concrete for adhesion.

Prime or undercoat

First coat may be thinned 10% with Cloud White Spirit to aid penetration on porous concrete. Follow with one to two full-strength coats.

Apply by brush or roller. Stir well before use. Allow full recoat interval between coats.
